51401066.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human RXR-alpha by ITC analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements were performed using a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical, Worcestershire, U.K.). The hRXRα-LBD (10 μM) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, and 0.02% (v/v) Tween 20. The ligand (7 or 14) was dissolved in DMSO and diluted with the same buffer to a final concentration of 100 μM. The protein solution (150 μL) was placed in the sample cell, and the ligand solution (200 μL) was loaded into the syringe. The experiment was performed at 25 °C with a stirring speed of 750 rpm. The ligand was injected in 20 steps of 2 μL each, with a 120 s interval between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA) with a one-site binding model. The blank experiment was performed by titrating the ligand into the buffer without the protein.
original_paragraph.Table 2 caption: aAt least three measurements were made for each sample. Values are mean ± SD (n = 3).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: CD and UV spectra of hRXRα-LBD in the absence (black) or presence of 3 (gray, dotted line), 7 (green), 12 (blue), and 14 (orange). (A) CD spectra of complexes at 190–260 nm, reflecting the secondary structure of hRXRα-LBD. Minima at 208 and 222 nm are observed. (B) Induced CD spectra of compounds at 250–350 nm. (C) [θ]222 and [θ]208 indicate the CD value at 222 and 208 nm, respectively. Values are mean ± SD. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01 (Bonferroni test, vs hRXRα-LBD only). (D) UV spectra of complexes. Values are the mean of three experiments.

assay_conditions.control_method: Titration of ligand into buffer without the protein
